record.name: South Africa
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. The draft AI policy, including a National AI Safety Institute proposal, was gazetted on 10 April 2026; withdrawal was announced on 26 April and formally took effect on 12 June 2026.

next_check.reason: Revised national AI policy is expected from the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies; check whether it proposes a safety institute.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. Recorded English and national or official-language queries and retrieved primary governance evidence support medium confidence. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

News search from 17 October 2026 in English and Afrikaans, with the communications department's media listing (newest 12 May, out of date) and the science department's account of 3 November. Left for review: the 3 November account of a 29 October dialogue with Finland, saying the department continues revising the withdrawn AI policy with an independent expert panel, and a TechCentral report of 29 October giving the timetable of revised policy to the minister by 30 November and a Cabinet submission in March 2027 for public consultation. No replacement policy or reinstated institute proposal was found, and support for the Finland and Norway call is not Network membership. The parliamentary reply of 14 October, which gives the March 2027 target, was read, but its printed page numbers could not be checked. Partial check, not a full record re-check.

check.language_note: English is an official language or an official language of national administration; it is a practical national search language for this check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: The withdrawal instrument and TimesLIVE article concern the same underlying policy withdrawal. A separately investigated institutional assessment was not established. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence.
check.governance_note: The official gazette withdraws the draft AI policy in full and the government account explains the decision. Withdrawn draft institutions are not treated as established.

record.notes:
The withdrawn draft proposed a National AI Safety Institute. Cabinet supported revising the policy in May 2026; no adopted replacement establishing such an institute was identified.

The communications department is revising the national AI policy and developing implementation roadmaps alongside it, the science department reported on 3 November 2026; the communications minister's reply to a parliamentary question, dated 14 October, aims to submit a revised policy to Cabinet by March 2027, and TechCentral reported on 29 October that the drafting team has a deadline of 30 November to submit to the minister, by which it must complete the revised policy and a discussion document.
